_comment: Original one-to-two sentence blurbs for /library/ (written for this site, keyed by book id). Never paste book text here: the site links to the source instead of republishing the stories.
369: Manu gets a bright new raincoat and can't wait for the rain to come so he can wear it. A gentle, repetitive story about waiting that little ones join in with.
2: A speedy fawn races through the forest until a stumble brings tears. Everyone tries to cheer him up, and his own kind words at the end make everyone laugh.
98: A little girl insists she is all grown up on her first day of school, but it turns out to be a big day for Mummy too. Perfect before a first day of school or kindergarten.
7: A fat king, his thin dog and a bird lead each other on a chase. Very short sentences and lots of repetition make it an ideal first book to read alone.
12294: Four friends line up their toy car, auto, bus and lorry for a race, until someone unexpected joins in. A counting-colours book with a funny twist.
16411: Shanu is too big for some things and too small for others. Every family member has an opinion, and Shanu has to figure out where he fits.
1042: A girl's best friend laughs when she laughs and cries when she cries, and lives somewhere surprising. A gentle riddle that ends in dreams.
49: Two best friends go fishing and hook the very same enormous fish, and neither will let go. A funny story with a splashy ending.
37232: Little Bee is lost, and a kind elephant helps her check nest after nest to find her home. A gentle, repeating story about helping. From Room to Read.
351358: Snails, fish, pigs and more come together in little rhymes, and each page asks: how many can you see? An early maths picture book with addition built in.
36641: Three little kittens are scared of a big dog, so they run, and run, and run. But the dog has a surprise for them. From Room to Read.
11537: A child's favourite hiding place is the big mango tree in Grandma's village garden. A short, sunny story about family visits.
10118: Sooraj wants coconut barfi, and his grandmother Ammachi agrees if he helps. Along the way the book shows the simple machines, like levers and wedges, hiding in her kitchen.
1281: Why is the homework not done? It's all the cat's fault, explains a child in one long, very creative chain of excuses.
10115: Neema loves food and is always eating. A playful book about eating habits that ends with a guide to which fruits and vegetables are in season when.
39753: Rabbit is tired of eating raw carrots every day, so she decides to learn to cook. Pairs nicely with the kitchen in the game.
44659: Meera and her invisible friend Ameera are a team, and Ameera turns every day into a big adventure. A tender, funny story about imaginary friends.
355071: It's the first day of the holidays, and two siblings may choose anything they like at the sweet shop. The hardest part is deciding.
14838: Peter disobeys his mother and squeezes into Mr. McGregor's garden. Beatrix Potter's most famous tale, with her original watercolours.
14407: Peter's cousin Benjamin talks him into going back to Mr. McGregor's garden to fetch his lost clothes. Things don't go to plan.
14872: Cheeky Squirrel Nutkin teases Old Brown the owl with riddles while his brothers gather nuts. A tale about a tail.
14814: Jemima Puddle-Duck wants to hatch her own eggs and sets off to find a secret nest, where a very polite gentleman offers to help.
14837: Mrs. Tabitha Twitchit dresses her three kittens in their best clothes for a tea party. Keeping them clean proves impossible.
15077: Mr. Jeremy Fisher the frog goes fishing in his lily-leaf boat, and the pond has a few surprises for him.
15137: Lucie keeps losing her pocket-handkerchiefs, and her search leads her to the tiny kitchen of Mrs. Tiggy-Winkle, a very special washerwoman.
14868: A poor tailor falls ill before finishing the mayor's wedding coat, and the mice he once saved come to help. A Christmas favourite.
14220: Benjamin Bunny's children, the Flopsy Bunnies, eat so much lettuce that they fall fast asleep in Mr. McGregor's rubbish heap.
45264: Two mice, Tom Thumb and Hunca Munca, explore a beautiful doll's house and are very disappointed by the food. A funny tale of mischief and making amends.
